items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the insurance law, in relation to providing enhanced consumer protections in the event of an insurer's discontinuance of coverage
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6263

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the insurance law, in relation to providing enhanced
consumer protections in the event of an insurer's discontinuance of
coverage


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
Bans discontinuance of entire classes of health insurance policies as
a pretext for dropping an individual policyholder, requires insurers
to prove that they are not dropping a class of policies as a pretext
for dropping an individual policyholder, empowers consumers by giving
them a private right of action against insurers who violate the new
law, and ensures that discontinued policyholders with severe illnesses
and disabilities have at least 18 months of free coverage if their
coverage is legitimately discontinued.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
This bill amends Section 3221(p) and 4305(j) of the Insurance Law to:
(1) create a prior approval process by the Insurance Department for
commercial and non-profit small and large group health insurers
seeking to discontinue a class of policies in New York State; (2) ban
insurers from discontinuing a class of policies if they are doing it
with the intent or as a pretext to dropping an individual
policyholder; (3) create a private rights of action for former
policyholders against insurers who violate the new law; and (4)
mandate that seriously ill or disabled policyholders who belong to a
class of policies that are legitimately discontinued receive free
coverage from the insurer for at least 18 months.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Existing law currently protects consumers by banning insurance
companies from dropping them due to their claims experience or health
status. However, there is currently a loophole which allows insurance
companies to drop coverage for an entire class of policyholders due to
one high cost individual;

Ian Pearl was a victim of that loophole. Mr. Pearl requires 24-hour
nursing care due to muscular dystrophy - a benefit that had been
covered by his insurance company. His insurance company admittedly
took the claims history of Mr. Pearl and other severely ill and
disabled policyholders into account when deciding which class of
policies to terminate, and referred to policyholders like Mr. Pearl as
"dogs" they could get rid of. This bill will ensure that no one
covered under a New York State insurance policy loses their coverage
due to their claims experience or health status, or the claims
experience or health status of another insured in their class of
policies.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.

B.actClause: AN ACT to amend the insurance law, in relation to providing enhanced consumer protections in the event of an insurer's discontinuance of coverage
B.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6263B

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the insurance law, in relation to providing enhanced
consumer protections in the event of an insurer's discontinuance of
coverage


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
Closes an existing loophole in New York State Insurance Law which
allows health insurance companies to discontinue entire classes of
policies as a pretext to dropping a high-cost individual's insurance
policy.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
This bill amends Section 3221(p) and 4305(j) of the Insurance Law to:

(1) require insurers to certify to the Insurance Department that they:
(i) provided written notice to all individuals covered by an affected
class of policies that they wish to discontinue a class of policies;
(ii) offered each policyholder in the class the option to purchase any
other medical coverage currently being offered by the insurer; and
(iii) are not dropping a class of policies as a pretext or with the
intent to dropping an individual policyholder;

(2) create a review process by the Insurance Department Superintendent
which can be triggered by policyholders submitting evidence that an
insurer is dropping a class of policies as a pretext or with the
intent to dropping an individual policyholder;

(3) create a private right of action for policyholders against
insurers who do not follow the proper procedure for discontinuing a
class of policies; and

(4) extend by six months the time period that policy holders with a
total disability, who lose coverage as part of the discontinuance of a
class of policies, shall receive continued coverage from the insurer
if no similar coverage is available.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Existing law currently protects consumers by banning insurance
companies from dropping them due to their claims experience or health
status. However, there is currently a loophole which allows insurance
companies to drop coverage for an entire class of policyholders due to
one high cost individual.

Ian Pearl was a victim of that loophole. Mr. Pearl requires 24-hour
nursing care due to muscular dystrophy - a benefit that had been
covered by his insurance company, issued in the state of New York as
part of a small group policy. His insurance company allegedly took the
claims history of Mr. Pearl and other severely ill and disabled
policyholders into account when deciding which class of policies to
terminate, and referred to cases like Mr. Pearl's as "dogs" they could
get rid of. This bill will provide an enforcement mechanism for the
current law that states that no one covered under an insurance policy
shall lose their coverage due to their claims experience or health
status, or the claims experience or health status of another insured
in their class of policies.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the first of January next succeeding the
date on which it shall have become a law and shall apply to all
policies and contracts issued, renewed, modified, altered or amended
on or after such effective date.

C.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S6263C

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the insurance law, in relation to providing enhanced consumer
protections in the event of an insurer's discontinuance of coverage

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:
Closes an existing loophole in New York State Insurance Law which
allows health insurance companies to discontinue entire classes of
policies as a pretext to dropping a high-cost individual's insurance
policy.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:
This bill amends Section 3221(p) and 4305(j) of the Insurance Law to:

(1) require insurers to certify to the Insurance Department that they:
(i) provided written notice to all individuals covered by an affected
class of policies that they wish to discontinue a class of policies;
(ii) offered each policyholder in the class the option to purchase any
other medical coverage currently being offered by the insurer; and
(iii) are not dropping a class of policies as a pretext or with the
intent to dropping an individual policyholder; and

(2) create a review process by the Insurance Department Superintendent
to ensure that policyholders with serious medical conditions who have
utilized benefits related to their serious medical condition within
the past 12 months get to keep coverage of those benefits when their
insurance company discontinues their class of policies.

JUSTIFICATION:
Existing law currently protects consumers by banning insurance
companies from dropping them due to their claims experience or health
status.
However, there is currently a loophole which allows insurance
companies to drop coverage for an entire class of policyholders due
to one high cost individual.

Ian Pearl was a victim of that loophole. Mr. Pearl requires 24-hour
nursing care due to muscular dystrophy - a benefit that had been
covered by his insurance company, issued in the state of New York as
part of a small group policy. His insurance company allegedly took
the claims history of Mr. Pearl and other severely ill and disabled
policyholders into account when deciding which class of policies to
terminate, and referred to cases like Mr. Pearl's as "dogs" they
could get rid of.

This bill will add a strong consumer protection mechanism for the
current law that states that no one with a serious medical condition
who is covered under an insurance policy shall lose their coverage of
benefits they have utilized in the last 12 months related to their

serious medical condition when their insurance company discontinues
their class of policies.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
New bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:
None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the first of January next succeeding the
date on which it shall have become a law.

summary: Enacts Ian's Law, which provides enhanced consumer protections in the event of an insurer's discontinuance of coverage, including requiring approval of the superintendent and notice to policyholders.
